meta_title: MacUp — Free Mac health check & cleaner in Terminal
meta_desc: Free, open-source Terminal tool for macOS: clear the hidden caches behind “System Data”, check SSD, battery, RAM, processor, graphics and security, and see your battery health % in a PDF report. No app, no subscription, Trash only.
og_title: MacUp — Your Mac’s health, right in Terminal. Free.
hero_lead: One command finds the hidden caches behind “System Data”, checks your SSD, battery, memory, processor, graphics and security — and saves a clear PDF health report in Downloads.
badge_free: No app · No account · No subscription
badge_trash: Trash only — nothing deleted for good
demo_lead: This is exactly what MacUp shows in Terminal. Press play or pick a chapter.
demo_cap_1: Smart Clean shows every hidden cache with its size. Press Enter and the selected ones go to the Trash.
demo_cap_2: This Mac: storage, SSD health, battery health and cycles, memory, processor and graphics on one screen.
demo_cap_3: Protection checks the security already built into macOS — read-only, with where to switch things on.
demo_cap_4: Performance shows the load, the busiest apps and startup items left behind by deleted apps.
demo_cap_5: Complete check runs everything: your battery health %, Good or Needs attention for each part, and what to do.
demo_cap_6: …and saves a three-page PDF report in your Downloads folder.
demo_note: Example values — your Mac shows its own numbers.
step1_d: Press ⌘ Space, type “Terminal” and press Enter.
step2_d: It installs MacUp in your home folder. No password, nothing runs in the background.
step3_d: Choose 1–5, press q to quit. Remove it any time with macup uninstall.
f1_d: Finds app caches, browser caches, logs, crash reports and 30+ developer caches. Shows sizes first, then moves your choice to the Trash.
f2_d: Storage used and free, SSD model and S.M.A.R.T. status, battery health %, cycles and charge, RAM and swap, processor cores, load and heat, graphics and displays.
f3_d: Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection, FileVault, firewall, XProtect, security responses and automatic updates — on or off.
f4_d: Load, the busiest apps by processor and memory, startup items, and broken startup items left by deleted apps.
f5_d: Everything above: your battery health %, Good or Needs attention for each part, and a three-page PDF report in Downloads.
f6_d: Empties Apple menu → Recent Items (apps, documents, servers) — the same as Clear Menu. Your files and apps stay where they are.
ghost_title: Hidden caches — not a broken Mac
ghost_lead: macOS keeps caches, logs and crash reports in hidden folders. Over months they grow to many gigabytes and show up in Settings as “System Data”. Apps rebuild them by themselves, so clearing them is safe.
ghost_no_reset_t: No need to format or reset your Mac
ghost_no_reset_d: Erasing a Mac to win back space takes hours and you have to restore everything. Clearing caches takes a minute — and it all goes to the Trash first, so you can put it back.
report_title: Battery health % and a clear PDF report
report_lead: macup check shows your battery health % — like on iPhone — and saves a three-page PDF in Downloads, easy to keep, print or share.
report_weights_note: The big number is your battery health (Macs without a battery show the SSD instead). Every other part gets a plain status:
report_p3: What to do, step by step
report_hw_d: RAM, SSD, battery, graphics and processor — with a clear status and, if something is wrong, the exact fix or command.
av_title: Does a Mac need a paid antivirus?
av_lead: For most people, no. Every Mac already includes free protection that Apple updates automatically. A yearly “virus cleaner” subscription doesn’t make it stronger.
av_builtin_t: Already built into your Mac — free
av_xprotect: Apple’s malware scanner, updated in the background
av_filevault: Encrypts your disk if the Mac is lost
av_responses: Urgent security fixes install by themselves
av_scam_t: “Your Mac is infected!” pop-ups are scams
av_scam_d: Close the tab. Don’t call the number, don’t install what it offers, don’t pay.
av_helps_t: What really keeps a Mac safe
av_help_2: Install apps from the App Store or developers you trust
av_help_3: Keep FileVault and the firewall on — macup protect shows both
av_note: MacUp is not an antivirus. It shows whether the protection already in macOS is switched on.
cmp_r_report: Health report (SSD, battery, RAM, CPU, GPU)
v_easy_delete: Easy to delete for good by mistake
cmp_note: A general comparison of product types, not of any specific company.
safe_title: Built so you can’t lose files
s1_d: Cleaning moves files to the Trash. MacUp never empties it and never deletes for good.
s2_d: Developer cleanup is an allowlist. Downloaded AI models, Xcode archives and anything that deletes for good are never offered.
s3_d: This Mac, Protection, Performance and the complete check only read. They never change settings.
s4_d: Runs as you, only while you use it. No admin password, no login items, no telemetry.
s5_d: If an app is using a file right now, MacUp leaves it alone.
s6_d: Every line is on GitHub. Read install.sh before you run it — it’s short.
a1: Yes. It’s open source under the MIT license — no trial, no subscription, no account, no ads.
q2: Why Terminal and not an app?
a2: A Terminal tool is small and transparent: no installer, no admin password, no background process. You can read every line it runs.
q3: Is it safe to clear caches?
a3: Yes. Caches are copies that apps rebuild by themselves. MacUp moves them to the Trash, so nothing is lost until you empty it, and files in use are skipped.
q4: Will I lose passwords, bookmarks or documents?
a4: No. MacUp never touches documents, photos, passwords or bookmarks. “Browser history only” is optional and off by default.
q5: Why don’t I see my SSD’s life %?
a5: macOS only reports S.M.A.R.T. Verified or Failing. Install the free smartmontools once and MacUp shows the life left %:
q6: Does it work on Intel Macs?
a6: Yes — macOS 13 Ventura or newer, on Apple silicon and Intel.
q7: How do I update or remove it?
a7: macup update installs the latest version. macup uninstall removes it completely; your PDF reports stay in Downloads.
a8: No. It works offline and has no telemetry. This website uses no cookies and no trackers.
